focus: Attacking the top rows and correcting four decisions
noveltyJustification: Four findings are new facts (emoji ranges, case-insensitivity, the section/never-move conflict, the draft-file count) and eight are re-ranking or attack analysis; (4 + 0.5*8) / 12 = 0.667, reported as 0.68.
keyQuestions: Which layout, colour, shape, density and label limits does the corpus treat as enforceable versus advisory, and do they support or contradict Flow Mode's limits (TD only, 9 nodes, 3 decision exits, one accent colour, four shapes)?

label: Emoji range corrected to ompug's published ranges, which include the checkmark inside the dingbat block.
Reserved-ID matching corrected to case-insensitive, withdrawing iteration 14's exact-match advice.
Thick edges are stylistic rather than semantic, but should still be rejected because Flow Mode already has colour as its one emphasis channel.
Dashed and undirected edges have legitimate uses elsewhere but not in Flow Mode, so the error message must name the label or loop alternative.
The section rule collides with the generator-owns-layout rule, because section placement reparents generated nodes.
Resolution: allow one organizational move into a named section without changing relative geometry, and keep the ban on rearranging.
The page rule's replacement is file-level: a new file or an existing fileKey, with an optional section, and no page language at all.
fileKey reuse moves to rank 3 because every regeneration without it creates a draft file.
Delete the previous diagram's nodes via use_figma, then regenerate with the same fileKey, replacing the cleared-page recovery recipe.
Section idempotency by name lets the read-back scope counts to the section's children.
The edge rule survives all attacks and keeps rank 1.
Top five re-ranked: edge rule, section and file rule, fileKey reuse, emoji, reserved IDs; underscore moves to six.

reason: The corpus linter lowercases IDs before comparing, so case-insensitive matching is the only consistent rule.
